title: Chapter 114: Hai Ming Apartments
html:
The cheapest is 3,000?Chen Ge coughed, one hand straying toward the roughly 20,000 RMB in his backpack. Keeping his voice calm, he said, “Money isn’t the problem. The new scenario opens in a few days, so I need the mannequins quickly. You don’t have enough workers, but do you have the materials?”

“I do.” The owner looked puzzled by the question. “Give me a few extra days, and I’m sure you’ll be satisfied.”

“The Haunted House will open the new scenario for visitation the day after tomorrow; there can be no delay.”

“Business is poor. Didn’t you see the sign? I used to handle the designs while my employees did the fabrication. When the large orders stopped, I let everyone go to cut costs.” Unwilling to lose the commission, he added, “I can call them tonight and rush the order within a week.”

“A week is still too long; I need them the day after tomorrow.”

The owner sighed. “Even at full speed, I could deliver only three or four by then.”

“So you have materials but no labor.” Chen Ge set down his backpack. “Then lend me the workshop for twenty-four hours. You only need to prepare the supplies.”

“Huh?”

The conversation had taken a turn the owner did not understand. “Then what am I supposed to do?”

“Stand aside and watch.” Chen Ge flexed his fingers and surveyed the room. “You don’t have other customers. Once the workshop sells, you’ll dispose of the materials or sell them at a discount. You might as well rent me the space for a day. I’ll pay market price for everything I use.”

The logic was sound, though something about the proposal felt wrong. With nothing to lose, the owner reluctantly nodded. “All right, but I want a 10,000 RMB deposit. I’ll deduct the material costs and return whatever remains.”

“You have a deal.”

After paying, Chen Ge entered the work area. It was vast, with tools and equipment covering the floor.

“You sure you want to do this yourself?” The boss was still hesitant. “If you need it, I can help. After all, I’m free.”

“Then I’ll thank you in advance.” An internship at a toy factory had made Chen Ge familiar with the equipment. After inspecting the workshop and forming a plan, he called Inspector Lee.

“Uncle Lee, I have a favor to ask; it’s related to Mu Yang High School.”

“The case is closed. Why are you still obsessed with Mu Yang High School?” Every call from Chen Ge made Inspector Lee brace himself for bad news.

“It’s not related to the case, I just want to…”

“Stop involving yourself with that school.” Inspector Lee’s tone hardened. “The city investigation suggests the site had a darker history even before the school was built.”

“A darker history?” Chen Ge did not pursue it. “You misunderstand. I’m not interfering with police work. You told me an entire class died in an accident. Do you have a photograph of the twenty-four students?”

“Have you lost your mind? Why do you need something like that?”

“It’s important, but I can’t explain yet. I swear I mean no harm.” He intended to build bodies for twenty-four homeless spirits. In his own way, he was doing something charitable.

After a long silence, Inspector Lee said, “Don’t do anything stupid. Call me if you discover something. I’ll check the files.”

Chen Ge ended the call without another thought, but the conversation had left the owner speechless. After some hesitation, the man edged closer. “Are you a police officer?”

“No, have you prepared the materials?”

“Yes.” Even the owner’s tone had become respectful.

“All right. Let’s begin.” They started by preparing the clay. Ten minutes later, Inspector Lee sent the only class photograph in the files. It showed twenty-six people: a bespectacled old man seated in the center and twenty-five students behind him.

“This will be much easier with a reference.” Chen Ge thanked the owner and asked him to step back. He shaped a rough head from clay, then activated Dollmaker’s Talent.

With a succession of carving knives, he transformed the clay into a human head resembling one student in the photograph. His hands moved like butterflies, each blade used with effortless precision. The owner watched in disbelief; it was like seeing an art documentary at triple speed.

What does this man actually do for a living?Once the carving was complete, Chen Ge smoothed the head with a wet sponge. As the dust vanished beneath his practiced touch, the clay took on the texture of skin.

When the clay hardened, he coated it with plaster and set it aside. The mold needed at least an hour to dry, so he began the next head.

An hour and a half later, every clay model was finished. He opened the first hardened molds and lined them with latex to form the mannequins’ skin.

He inserted a flexible support to serve as the spine, then injected the filler. The entire process flowed in one practiced sequence. Each mannequin head took only ten minutes.

“It’s getting late. Take this 10,000 as the deposit, and don’t touch anything in the work area. I’ll be back to finish the rest tomorrow.” Chen Ge washed his hands and planned to leave for Hai Ming Apartments.

“Don’t worry. I won’t go near them.” The owner shivered at the twenty-four heads lining the counter. He had seen thousands of mannequins, but Chen Ge’s creations felt different. They looked ready to blink.

Chen Ge shouldered his backpack, left the underground workshop, and hailed a taxi to Hai Ming Apartments. It was almost time to meet Doctor Gao.

Hai Ming Apartments stood in an older district of low-rise buildings. Beyond several busy streets, the city grew quiet. Following the driver’s directions, Chen Ge reached his destination.
